title: Shipping a city builder to Steam EA in 2 months. 20k lines of JS, what worked and what didn't.
author: Realistic_Age6660

comments.author: Realistic_Age6660
comments.body:
What started as an idea on a hot summer's day in July is now going into Early Access on Steam next week. Isometric city builder set in the Khmer Empire - canals, monsoon flooding, and you build Angkor Wat across five missions.

  
Tech: around 20k lines of JavaScript.

  
What worked

  
\- AI makes changes really fast.

  
What didn't

  
\- Copy - AI is terrible at copywriting, even with reference material. I do have to go in and manually fix every line, which is a pain in the butt, although it's something I feel is necessary to fix.  
\- Meshy to Blender to 2D frame capture for building art. Every step increased room for error, so I killed that early.  
\- Automated testing framework: was useful early on, but later it was taking too long as small changes went from 5 minutes to an hour, so I killed it later.

  
The reception

  
Posted a 20 ish second clip to r/CityBuilders yesterday, and some people liked it but there's also an anti-AI thread in the comments which went about how you'd expect lol.

  
What I'd do next time  
\- Use AI only when I need to, like tricky technical code changes, or prototyping and keep more human say over the final product.

Store link for anyone interested: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5068280/Angkor/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5068280/Angkor/)

  
Thanks for reading!

replies.author: LucidFir
replies.body: ok i kinda love the idea of zero assets. any idea for me (i know nothing!) how to take the sprites of boats i had chatgpt make and get them done as vector art? i feel like it should be possible for an AI to recreate even a photo with just vectors... but I've no idea what problems that would create

replies.author: Realistic_Age6660
replies.body:
that's a good question - maybe i'll do a YouTube video on it?

short version: 2d art is either raster (pixels, which is what chatgpt images are) or vector (shapes and coordinates, which an LLM can just write as code). you might see this as a dot svg \[.svg\] files around the web e.g. brand logos. they're different things, so there's no clean conversion - you'd be tracing, and tracing an AI image gives you a traced AI image.

what worked for me was not making raster images (which had a high error rate). instead, I describe the building and ask for a draw function instead, then iterate on the code. your boats would be a drawBoat(ctx, x, y) that puts down a hull polygon, a mast line, a sail. takes more passes than generating a picture, but you get free scaling, recoloring and tweening out of it. I recommend something like Claude; I didn't have a good experience with ChatGPT although that might have changed with the new Astra 6 model (haven't tried it yet).

comments.author: oliganti
comments.body: You ditched tests for speed, was the tradeoff worth it? How about bugs after ditching it?

replies.author: Realistic_Age6660
replies.body: mixed. iteration got faster once I ditched tests, but I lost 'coverage', which AI kept telling me was important. I felt it was flawed though - it was brittle heuristics playing a game, which is inferior to a human playing or a trained NN like OpenAI Five, and I don't have the budget for a NN to learn the game lol. bug-wise it hasn't been much worse, and the bugs that do show up are mostly things tests wouldn't catch anyway - ui not being findable, balance, copy. they're all in git history if I need them, just not in the context window that gets passed to the AI.
